findings.summary: Help modal opens scrolled to the BOTTOM of its content on any viewport where the guide overflows — the user lands on 'Mechanics… Got it!' and never sees the 'Help Guide' title or Game Modes section.
findings.detail: openModal() calls _a11yFocusIntoModal(), whose only focusable in modal-help is the 'Got it!' button at the very end of the content (battle.html:10007); button.focus() scroll-anchors .modal-content to the bottom (measured scrollTop=399 of 399 max on phone, activeElement='Got it!'). Desktop is unaffected only because the content happens to fit in 900px. A first-time player asking for help starts reading from the end and may believe that's the whole guide.
findings.evidence: rig/out/home-shell/help-top-phone.png, help-top-phoneL.png (vs help-top-desktop.png showing intended top)
findings.fix: Focus with {preventScroll:true} then reset .modal-content.scrollTop=0 in showHelp, or give the h2/container tabindex=-1 and a [data-modal-autofocus] on it.

findings.summary: The headline 'POKéMON' logo wraps mid-word into 'POKéM / ON' on standard portrait phones — the first thing every mobile player sees is a broken title.
findings.detail: Phone override sets font-size: clamp(2.8rem, 13vw, 4.5rem) — at 390px that is 50.7px which, with letter-spacing 4px in Press Start 2P, makes the 7-glyph word wider than the column, so the h1 breaks into two lines (measured rect height 100px = 2 lines). ARENA below then reads 'POKéM ON ARENA'.
findings.fix: Lower the vw term (~11vw) or add white-space:nowrap plus a smaller clamp so the word always fits one line at 360-430px.

findings.summary: The 'Battle Options — teams, rules & bot difficulty' toggle wraps into 3 cramped lines at every viewport, with 'difficulty' nearly colliding with the line above and the chevron floating beside a text block.
findings.detail: The button is capped at max-width:320px with a 13px label and min-height:44px; the 43px-tall wrapped span leaves ~14px per line (near-zero leading for a pixel font). It looks broken even on a 1440px desktop where space is plentiful.
findings.fix: Shorten the label to 'Battle Options' with the long tail as a smaller sub-line, or raise max-width/allow height to grow with real line-height.

findings.summary: The Display select's selected value renders clipped as 'Auto (dete' at every viewport, including desktop where the row has abundant empty space.
findings.detail: Inline style caps the select at max-width:160px while the longest option is 'Auto (detect)'; native selects hard-clip the value with no ellipsis. Battle speed / Gimmick speed selects share the 160px cap but their options happen to fit.
findings.fix: Widen to fit the longest option (~200px) or shorten the option label to 'Auto'.

findings.summary: On tablet portrait the entire menu (logo, both primaries, mode grid, offline entry) is packed into the top ~50% of the display and the bottom half is empty arena background.

findings.summary: 'G1…G9' generation checkboxes and 'Grades: G1…G4' tier badges use the identical token 'G1-G4' for two different concepts a few rows apart in the same panel.

findings.summary: The 8px 'v1.6.1' version tag uses z-index 2147483646 and paints on top of every overlay and modal, including the app-loading overlay and settings sheet.

findings.summary: Confirm dialog always shows generic 'Cancel' / 'OK' with OK styled green, so destructive confirms (abandon run, spend gold) present the dangerous choice in the 'safe/positive' color with no verb.

findings.summary: The retired rotate-overlay still ships ~30 lines of markup/CSS/keyframes plus a JS boot hide; if it ever resurfaces, its 'icon' is a meaningless '▒' dither glyph rather than a rotate pictogram.
findings.detail: CSS default is display:none, a portrait media query redundantly sets display:none again (:4979), and checkOrientation() force-hides it at boot with a comment saying it's retired (:11202) — three layers agreeing it's dead while the DOM keeps it at z-index 9999.

clusters.designNotes: The front door is in decent shape and clearly post-redesign: one pixel typeface everywhere, a real primary pair (Story Mode + Jump In) above a labeled, demoted 'Quick Play & Multiplayer' section, preset chips gating the full options panel, and the settings bottom-sheet with proper switches is the most modern surface in the cluster. Nothing overflows horizontally even at 360px. What undercuts the first impression: (1) the POKéMON logotype wraps mid-word on every portrait phone — the single most visible defect in the game; (2) Help opens scrolled to its own footer on phones, which reads as broken; (3) the Battle Options toggle crams a 3-line sentence into a 44px chip on all viewports; and (4) tablet portrait leaves the bottom half of the screen dead. Hierarchy question from the brief: there are effectively TWO primary actions (Story Mode and Jump In share identical size/green treatment) — acceptable as a deliberate returning-vs-new split, but giving Story Mode slightly more weight (or the continue slot a filled style vs outlined Jump In) would resolve the tie. The expanded options panel is functional but the 11-hue rainbow of checkbox labels and the G1-G9-gens vs G1-G4-grades naming collision make it feel less designed than the settings sheet next to it. Alert/confirm modals are clean GBA-style cards; the confirm's green generic OK is the only semantics issue. Loading overlay is fine (spinner + status text), though the max-z version tag floats above it. Rotate overlay is dead code and should be excised.

clusters.designNotes: These entry surfaces are among the game's most polished: one pixel typeface throughout (Press Start 2P, zero font-family mixing), a coherent dark-navy palette with per-mode color coding (green=continue, red=new/danger, blue=collection), and strong CTA hierarchy on the story menu, defeat screen, and cold open. The three-step numbered trainer-create flow ('1 - Who's walking out of Pallet?') is genuinely good information architecture for a new player — the reading load is well-chunked, the Advanced section is correctly collapsed by default, and the '★ Recommended' badge plus pre-selected Normal makes the safe path obvious. The City-0 cold open is a confident, clean piece of staging on desktop and portrait phone. What undercuts the modern/clean read: (1) the difficulty microcopy — the one block of text that actually drives the new-player decision — is set at 7.5-8px, an order of magnitude below the rest of the hierarchy, so the screen's most important words are its least readable; (2) short-viewport robustness is poor — both the cold open and the defeat screen use fixed/flex-centered full-height layouts with no scroll fallback, which clips headings and strands buttons at 844x390; (3) the sticky Begin footer's half-transparent gradient lets scrolled content bleed through, reading as a collision rather than a designed fade; (4) the always-visible custom-gen grid (hidden-attr defeated by display:grid) makes step 3 look permanently 'expanded' and lets UI state silently contradict itself. Biggest wins for effort: one CSS line for the [hidden] fix, text-align on the story title, ~10px floor + shorter strings on diff cards, and overflow-y:auto + margin:auto centering on the two full-screen surfaces.

clusters.designNotes: The city hub is one of the strongest surfaces in the game: a single pixel typeface throughout, disciplined dark-navy card system with the gold accent reserved for affordable/active facilities, clear section headers with counts, and meaningful status pills (Free/New/Auto-Build/cost). The arrival card, route interstitial and wander screen are genuinely atmospheric and well-composed at every viewport - modern GBA-dark done right. The phone portrait stack and the touch-tablet stack are clean. What undercuts it: (1) overflow handling on the two rails - the desktop tips rail silently hides actionable suggestions in a wrapped phantom column, and the phone HUD pushes Settings/Help off-canvas entirely; these are the two real functional breaks. (2) Full-screen reader overlays (journal, errand dialogs) ghost the hub through their translucent backdrops, which reads as visual noise against otherwise crisp surfaces - one opaque backdrop fixes the whole class. (3) Density edge cases: 2-line facility names collapse their padding on desktop and stack awkwardly on phone - tier suffixes ('- Black Belt', '- Unleashed') would live better in the meta pill row. (4) The 9-9.5px meta layer (kickers, pills, counts) is below comfortable legibility and is where the known type-ramp work will pay off most here. Biggest wins in order: opaque overlay backdrops, tips-rail nowrap, HUD wrap on phone, then the 2-line-label card sizing.

clusters.designNotes: The commerce cluster is in better shape than the average of this codebase: the mart/dept shop grid is genuinely clean (uniform 34x34 icons, consistent left-price/right-Buy card anatomy, scannable category heads), the casino is the most art-directed surface in the game (themed felt per game, brass-halo titles, chunky pixel chips), and the phone roulette board — the flagged hotspot — actually fits with room to spare (180px wheel, 84x48 cells, zero overflow). The biggest wins available: (1) the Relic shop is the one broken layout — on 390px phones every card, the Buy button and the Browse/Manage tabs run ~23px off the right edge because the nowrap AFFECTS-BOTH-SIDES badge inflates grid min-content (grid items lack min-width:0); (2) the casino's cream-on-light-felt text family (ISSUE-026) is at its worst on the Coin Flip gold panel where the subtitle and odds line are close to invisible, and the same 'fade it out' instinct makes the disabled Spin button vanish into the green felt entirely; (3) the four shops speak three different price/CTA dialects (price-left+'Buy' vs 'Buy 500G' vs 'Price: X'+'Buy for X') — one card grammar would make the whole commerce layer feel like one system. Desktop roulette wastes its left half (a lone wheel floating in felt) while everything interactive stacks on the right. The GBA-dark aesthetic itself holds up well here; the issues are fit-and-finish, not direction.

clusters.designNotes: The tx-facility family (Tutor, Mentor, Colress, Link, Evolution Lab, EV Trainer, Fan Club) shares one coherent card/toggle/pill system and on desktop it genuinely reads modern and on-brand: Colress desktop, the Hidden Power picker, the daycare modal and the mentor intro cameo (dimmed scene + nameplate + Continue) are the strongest surfaces — clear hierarchy, dark navy + gold discipline, generous cards. Mentor's Auto-Build receipt (Moves/Item/Nature/EV rows with per-line costs and Total) is excellent information design. What drags the cluster down: (1) phone headers were never designed — every long facility title wraps (Colress catastrophically, Fan Club into a text collision), while the tutor's short title is fine, so the fix is one shared header component with truncation + demoted subtitle; (2) sticky chrome (mon switcher, filter toolbar, confirm bar) is layered but not opaque, producing double-exposure collisions the moment content scrolls — the single most 'broken-feeling' thing in the whole cluster; (3) a sub-10px badge layer (9/9.5px type badges, stat pills, cost badges) sits under everything and undermines the otherwise readable pixel type — raising the floor to 10-11px would cost little; (4) the flat .type-X color override repainting the tutor's slot chips is a regression that both breaks contrast and muddies the intended dark-chip aesthetic; (5) desktop space usage is uneven — EV Trainer stretches stat bars edge-to-edge while the professor squeezes three cards into the center; a shared max-content-width would unify them. Team Tester is the one surface with zero design language applied. Biggest wins in order: opaque sticky bars, shared phone facility header, revert type-color chip override, 10px text floor.

clusters.designNotes: This cluster is among the game's most polished: one pixel typeface everywhere, disciplined dark-navy surfaces with tier-colored card borders, strong dex/memorial hierarchy, and the populated Pokedex grid with silhouette-for-seen is genuinely charming and information-dense. What breaks the modern/clean read is the pixel font's unforgiving glyph width meeting fixed-width boxes: the two flagship defects (Withdraw/Release collision on every PC card; 'Resistec' on every Matchups card) are both 10px Press-Start-2P text physically wider than its 70-148px container, and they make otherwise-fine screens look broken at every viewport. Second theme: state hygiene — tab switches (Collection, PC Storage/Underground) keep stale scroll so screens open mid-list, and the landscape summary loses its only close affordance (P0 trap). Third: micro-type floor — 8-9.5px is used for real data (stats, dex numbers, captions) not just decoration, and white-on-type-color badges sit at 2-3:1. Biggest wins in order: (1) fix the three overflow/close bugs — pure CSS, huge perceived-quality lift; (2) reset scroll on tab change; (3) establish a 10px minimum with per-type badge ink colors; (4) reclaim dead space (grip band, 5+1 tablet party grid, 460px party modal on desktop).

clusters.designNotes: The battle screen is in much better shape than the old responsive-layout audit describes: the rebuilt 2-template system (arena/stack, single JS switch, container-query sizing) produces a genuinely clean GBA-dark look on desktop, laptop and portrait phone — consistent pixel typeface, coherent navy palette with gold accents, well-composed command grid with color-coded actions and keyboard hints, readable field-pill row, and a tasteful minimal end screen. Weather/terrain overlays (sandstorm stripes, electric grid) and status chips are the visual high point. The two worst things are both edge-template failures rather than styling: landscape-touch arena hides the player HP card entirely (P0 — the single biggest fix available), and tablet portrait's 250px bottom bar lets the log squeeze the command grid into clipping. The next tier is small-screen typography: the game leans on 9px (and 8px) pixel text for almost everything secondary — log, badges, meta rows — which at phone DPRs is legible but at the absolute floor, and white-on-type-color chips fail contrast; move-tile names disintegrate below 400px ('Sola r…'). Space usage is generally good in stack (phone portrait is the best-designed viewport); arena on 16:10/4:3 letterboxes gracefully. Biggest wins in order: (1) unhide the landscape player card, (2) give the command grid height priority over the log on tablet, (3) a 3-step type ramp with 10px floor + dark-text type chips, (4) name-first space allocation in compact HUD cards, (5) disable the dead BAG slot in Quick Play.

census.note: runChecks scans the whole visible DOM; on camp overlays the counts include the dimmed underlying home-menu (menu-mode-btn etc.) bleeding through the rgba(0,0,0,0.95) shell — camp-specific values summarized here, raw per-screen JSON in rig/out/camp-minigames/checks-{desktop,phone,tablet,phoneL,phoneS}.json
census.reducedMotionCoverage: countdown pulse gated by _campReduceMotion (battle.html:59268-59272); mastery/title FxParticles burst documented no-op under reduced motion (battle.html:59206-59217); remaining microgame motion (markers, drifting dots, falling berries) is gameplay-essential and exempt-appropriate; camp CSS itself adds no prefers-reduced-motion blocks (31 exist app-wide)
census.reflexFairness360px: time windows are viewport-independent by construction — tapTiming/gaugeStop positions are track-fractions over a fixed period (green-zone dwell = zoneHalf*period ≈ 77-176ms regardless of width), dodge/goNoGo windows are ms-based, and px tolerances (dragAim radius 26-50px, trace tol 22-40px) stay constant while fields shrink via vw, so 360px is actually slightly more forgiving; nothing reflex-based gets harder on small screens

clusters.designNotes: The camp suite is one of the most coherent-feeling corners of the game: the hub's night-gradient + firelight cast is a genuinely lovely beat, the gold-bordered scene cards keep the pixel typeface and amber accent consistent, the 3-2-1-GO countdown surfaces each game's name and instructions BEFORE the clock starts (the single best readability decision here — instructions are never read under time pressure), and the 30-game toolkit is impressively legible on a 360px phone with fair, time-based (viewport-independent) reflex windows. What undercuts it: (1) game pieces are stock emoji — human lips 👄 as the Feed target, 🐱 critters, 💣 bombs, 🧺 baskets — which read as placeholder art against the GBA-dark pixel aesthetic; sprite-based or pixel-drawn pieces would lift the whole suite; (2) place-continuity breaks the moment you tap into the roster because sub-scenes drop the campfire backdrop/cast; (3) the two catch screens (wild + safari) degrade badly in phone landscape, hiding every action below an unhinted fold — the one real P1 here; (4) accessibility is an afterthought inside the games: color-only sequence pads, wrong copy-paste aria-labels, no quit affordance; these are small, contained fixes. Minor polish: Cheer and Feed & Groom share the same 😊 emoji so the six action rows read as five moods; the '·×2 ✓' suffix soup on favoured/mastered action labels is cramped; the loss result card is well-toned (clear ✕, red accent, no punishment). Biggest wins in order: clamp the stage height on short viewports, label the sequence pads, add a quit button to the microgame shell, carry the campfire backdrop through all camp sub-scenes.

findings.summary: In touch-landscape the entire player HP panel (name, HP bar, status, party balls) is clipped invisible — the player fights blind while the foe panel renders fine.
findings.detail: #battle-player-hud-row is absolutely positioned above its parent's top edge in arena layout (bottom: calc(var(--battle-ui-h)+...) puts it at y=167 while #battle-bottom-stack spans y=234..390), and the touch-landscape media query sets `body.is-mobile #screen-battle .battle-bottom-stack { overflow: hidden; }`, so the row is 100% clipped. Probe: row rect t=167 h=64, clipping ancestor #battle-bottom-stack t=234 h=156 overflow:hidden position:relative. Reproduced in gauntlet and quick battle; desktop/tablet/portrait unaffected.
findings.anchor: battle.html:306-309 (`body.is-mobile #screen-battle .battle-bottom-stack, .ui-bottom { overflow: hidden; }` in the landscape+coarse @media) vs :3939 (`.battle-bottom-stack { position: relative }` grid template) and :4384 (arena #battle-player-hud-row absolute placement)
findings.fix: Exclude .battle-bottom-stack from the landscape overflow:hidden rule (or move #battle-player-hud-row out of the stack in arena layout) so the absolutely-positioned player card can paint above the command bar.

findings.summary: Fight Club overlay's top (the '🥊 FIGHT CLUB' title and first-rule strapline) is clipped above the viewport and can never be scrolled into view when the card is taller than the screen.
findings.detail: Classic align-items:center + overflow-y:auto trap: the overlay centers a 946px-tall card in an 844px viewport, so the top overhang is outside the scrollable range. Probe at scrollTop=0: card top = -51px, ov.scrollHeight 915 < content need. On phoneL the entire header including title is unreachable. Also an E1-pattern DIY fixed div rather than a .modal.
findings.fix: Use align-items:flex-start (or safe centering via `margin:auto` on the card child) so tall content scrolls from its true top.

findings.summary: Reaching the Hall of Fame fires up to 5 achievement toasts simultaneously; the stacked column covers the HoF ceremony text and the CONTINUE (POST-GAME)/END RUN buttons, and toasts are pointer-events:auto so they also block taps beneath.
findings.detail: _storyRecordHallOfFame grants first_hof/r_hof/champion-career/no-death/flawless in one tick and each calls _storyAchievementToast → showToast(…, 3800). #toast-host is a bottom-anchored full-width column with centered items, so 5 multi-line toasts stack up over mid-screen. On phone they hide nearly the whole card; on desktop they sit exactly over the welcome copy and the CONTINUE button. Reproduced via previewHallOfFame on a fresh meta, which is the same state as a player's genuine first HoF.
findings.fix: Queue achievement toasts sequentially (or collapse simultaneous grants into one 'x achievements unlocked' toast), and/or suppress toasts while the HoF overlay is up.

findings.summary: When the Supabase JS client is absent (the default local/offline state) the leaderboard modal shows a raw JS exception — 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading createClient)' — instead of the friendly setup message.
findings.detail: openGauntletLeaderboardModal only shows the friendly 'Add Supabase keys…' copy when __onlinePvpConfigured() exists and returns false; when window.supabase itself is undefined the try/catch dumps e.message into #gauntlet-lb-err verbatim. Players see engineer-speak inside a game modal.
findings.fix: Map all failure paths (missing lib, missing keys, network) to the same friendly 'online leaderboard not configured/unreachable' message and keep the raw error in console only.

findings.summary: All 19 Crucible action buttons carry their only explanations (what each battle/facility does, stakes, costs) in title attributes — invisible on touch devices and effectively lost to most users.
findings.detail: Verified programmatically: 19/19 buttons in #story-crucible-body have >20-char title-only help (e.g. 'Endless 6v6 ladder. One loss ends the run; final streak goes to the Top-10.'). Phone/tablet are primary targets; there hover never fires, so a post-game player picking between six battle modes gets label-only buttons.

findings.summary: The floating settings gear overlaps the foe panel's party-ball indicators in portrait battle — the topmost ball is half-hidden and a tap on it opens Settings.

findings.summary: The 'My picks' tray ellipsizes species names at ~6 characters ('Dewgong' → 'Dewgo…') and its remove '×' affordance is ~12px — long names like Basculegion become unidentifiable.

findings.summary: The gauntlet draft is visually identical to the quick-battle draft — header says only 'Pick 3 Pokémon for your Team' with no indication you are entering the survival ladder.

clusters.designNotes: Two distinct styling eras coexist in this cluster. The story-era endgame surfaces — Crucible hub, Frontier hub, Fight Club overlay, Hall of Fame card, mystery-climax scenes — are the modern face of the game: consistent header rows (back arrow / icon+title / gold), uppercase section kickers with letter-spacing, soft translucent card grids, per-mode accent borders, and they scale cleanly from phone portrait to desktop. The Crucible hub in particular is the best-organized screen I audited (clear Battles vs Facilities hierarchy, sensible 2-col grid), let down only by its help text living entirely in hover-only title attributes. The quick-play surfaces (draft screen, gauntlet swap, leaderboard modal, end screen) are visibly an older era: white-outline modals with hard #333 borders, inline styles, bare yellow h2s, denser 9-11px text and unlabeled edge-to-edge layout — they function fine but don't share the story screens' chrome language, spacing rhythm, or radius scale. Biggest wins in order: (1) the phone-landscape battle clip that hides the player's own HP panel (P0, one-line CSS cause); (2) sequencing the Hall-of-Fame achievement toast dump so the ceremony reads as a ceremony; (3) the overlay scroll pattern (margin:auto instead of align-items:center) for Fight Club and any tall DIY overlay; (4) porting the story-era card/header language onto the draft + swap + end-screen so Gauntlet/Quick no longer feel like a different product; (5) the end screen is very spartan for a game this polished — a 'Play again' CTA for quick battles and a streak recap for gauntlet would close the loop instead of always bouncing to the main menu. Frontier hub desktop also leaves ~60% dead space in its empty state; seeding the Top-10 panel with a ghost row or centering a max-width column would help.

findings.summary: The mandatory first battle of the game (rival starter duel, party of 1) is lose-heavy on Normal for a naive player: this pass lost in 2 moves; a prior naive-play pass hit 4 consecutive DEFEATED screens before a damage-optimal strategy won.

clusters.designNotes:
PLAYTEST REPORT — brand-new player, phone-first (390x844, touch, no harness, real pacing), then desktop 1440x900 for the first 10 beats, plus tablet/phoneL spot passes and a Quick Battle pass.

WAYFINDING: genuinely strong. At no beat did I have to hunt for the next action — the START/NEXT quest banner ('Pick your starter at the Lab ▶', 'Rival — starter duel at the gate ▶'), the SUGGESTED chips, and reason-labeled gates ('Continue Route (Visit Pokémart first)' shown disabled with the reason inline) form a clear rail. NEW/FREE/REQUIRED chips on facility cards are excellent affordance. This is the best part of the new-player experience and worth protecting.

PACING & READING LOAD: home → City 0 is 9 taps / ~20s at rig pace; first battle is 17 taps and 9 separate text surfaces (cold open, welcome alert, clerk overlay, ball alert, Oak x3 pages, banter x2). With typewriter effects and honest reading, a real player reaches their first battle in roughly 3-5 minutes — acceptable for a story game, but the text is fragmented across four different overlay styles with four different dismiss verbs, so it feels busier than it is. The City Guide typewriter runs ~5+ seconds per quote; two of my arrival screenshots caught it mid-word, meaning players routinely start scrolling before the flavor line finishes (not a bug, but consider a faster reveal or tap-to-complete).

THE WALL: the first mandatory fight (rival duel, party of 1) is brutally lose-heavy for naive play — I lost in 2 moves this pass, and the prior naive pass ate FOUR consecutive DEFEATED screens. The defeat screen itself is the best-designed screen in the funnel (clear hierarchy: Retry / Concede-with-cost / Return / Delete), but 'game over inside minute one of combat, repeatedly' is the single biggest new-player churn risk I found, compounded by the banter choice silently gambling ±5% damage right before it. Meanwhile Quick Battle is 1 tap → fighting in ~4s — a fantastic instant on-ramp (only blemish: the always-dead BAG command).

MODERN/CLEAN VERDICT: desktop reads beautifully — the city hub at 1440px is a tidy, hierarchical dashboard; battle is clean GBA-dark with a confident gold accent; mart/relic screens are strong card layouts. Phone is where polish breaks: three HUD controls clipped off-screen on the primary story screen, the sticky create-footer eating the run-option toggles, relic cards clipping 9px, the wordmark wrapping mid-word, 7.5px microtype on the difficulty choice, and in landscape the player's own HP plate simply doesn't exist. Pattern: desktop-tuned absolute/sticky positioning + overflow:hidden containers failing at 390px. Biggest wins, in order: (1) fix the three phone reachability/clipping bugs (HUD actions, create footer, phoneL player plate) — they are mechanical, not aesthetic; (2) soften or teach through the first rival fight; (3) unify the five overlay presentation styles and their dismiss verbs; (4) lift the sub-10px text on the two screens where a new player makes real decisions (difficulty cards, battle meta).

Help (489-533) and Settings (541-585) fully off-screen; #screen-story-city and body overflow-x:hidden, no scrollable ancestor, elements untappable. verified.note: Rig artifact. The 'occluded' inputs (story-mech-dyna/tera, story-mode-classic/unlimited-rb, story-no-item-run) are children of the CLOSED <details class="story-create-advanced"> (battle.html:10830) — Chromium retains layout geometry for closed-details content, so probes see nonzero rects for controls that are not painted or tappable at all. I reproduced the original probe's exact numbers (maxScroll=494, same IDs) only in the closed state. With the accordion open (the only state where those controls exist for the player), maxScroll grows to 777 and ZERO controls sit behind/below the Begin bar at max scroll — v3c-create-open-maxscroll.png shows every control fully clear of the CTA. The gen-checkbox 'half-clipped' screenshot was ordinary mid-scroll sticky-footer overlay that clears on further scroll (v3b-create-closed-maxscroll.png).

verified.summary: The mandatory first battle of the game (rival starter duel, party of 1) is lose-heavy on Normal for a naive player: this pass lost in 2 moves; a prior naive-play pass hit 4 consecutive DEFEATED screens before a damage-optimal strategy won.
verified.note: Not reproducible as a general property. I re-drove the full real new-player flow twice (harness:false) with a maximally naive first-listed-move policy: roll 1 (Abra) WON despite wasting 10 turns on Protect; roll 2 (Nidoran-M) WON in 3 moves using a move the UI itself flagged ▼ resisted. The auditor's 4 'consecutive' defeats were retries of the SAME matchup roll (journey-phone-6.mjs retry loop), not independent samples, and their other loss carried a self-inflicted −5% Flirt dialogue penalty. The fix rationale is factually wrong: the 'Your First Fight' tutorial (battle.html:50293-50299, STORY_TUTORIAL_SCENES.firstTrainerBattle) explicitly teaches the claimed-missing control — '"...you'll see ▲ super-effective, ▼ resisted, ⊘ no effect. Chase the ▲."' — and the battle-log tip repeats '▲▼ = damage matchup'. Residual kernel (some starter rolls lose their counter-matchup with naive play) is per-roll variance in maintainer-owned balance numbers per CLAUDE.md, not a confirmed UX defect.

codeAudits.designNotes: The bones are genuinely good: one pixel typeface shipped (Press Start 2P + monospace fallback — a true single-typeface product, rare), a dark-navy surface ramp, gold accent, a 6-tier z ladder, motion/easing/radius/text tokens all DEFINED as of the 2026-07-04 PR, and 108 custom properties total. What reads un-modern is not the aesthetic but the entropy: 859 unique hexes (mostly ad-hoc Material 300/400 picks), 247 unique box-shadows, 71 unique transitions, ~94 button classes, and 1597 inline styles mean no two screens share an exact vocabulary — the casino, tutor (tx-*), and story-narrative (sn-*) sub-systems each re-invented chips, tabs, bevels, and gold. The single most important observation of this census: THE TOKEN LAYER HAS ~0% ADOPTION (--dur-* 4 uses, --radius-* 2, --text-dim 0) while 510 hex occurrences literally spell out token values by hand — the system was built but never swept in, and it is drifting backward (+250 inline styles, +28 button classes, +3 breakpoints, +13 font !importants since R5). Biggest wins in order of leverage-per-risk: (1) the zero-risk mechanical session — exact-hex→token sed (510), 0.12s/0.15s→--dur (99), half-px font rounding (23) — cuts headline numbers ~20% in an afternoon with no visual change; (2) the gray-ramp alias sweep, which is simultaneously the R5 WCAG contrast fix; (3) the 6-family button consolidation with per-screen theme wrappers (casino keeps its felt-and-brass skin by overriding custom props, not by owning 10 classes) — that is the change a player would actually FEEL as 'this game got cleaner'.

codeAudits.designNotes: The 2026-07-04 UX PR genuinely landed its a11y items — this is now a far better-than-average canvas: all 26 screens carry role=region + human aria-labels (E5 verified); the modal system is complete (one guarded global Escape handler with data-no-escape opt-out = A7 shipped, global Tab trap, _a11yFocusIntoModal on open, focus-stack restore on close, promise-settling on generic dismissal); showScreen focuses the new region; renderCityActions preserves focus+scroll across re-renders (E3 shipped, battle.html~53950); a global :focus-visible gold ring (line 97) is clearly visible in screenshots; move buttons have exemplary aria-labels (name/type/cat/power/acc/PP/priority + numeric shortcut); the battle log is role=log and announces a complete turn narrative (verified: 'Persian used Double-Edge! / It dealt 127 damage! / ... / Persian fainted! / Foe sent out Togepi!'); quick-draft pool cards are the house pattern for clickable cards (role=button, tabIndex 0, keydown Enter/Space); settings switches now use label[for] (ISSUE-101 wave fixed); reduced-motion has 31 CSS blocks + StoryFx.isReducedMotion/_campReduceMotion/_mgReducedMotion JS gates. The remaining problem is UNEVENNESS: newer/peripheral flows (professor gift pick, battle bag, Pits picks, minigame overlays) were built as onclick-divs or focus-less dialogs and never got the house pattern, and one of them (professor pick) hard-blocks Story mode for keyboard users at its very first mandatory step. KEYBOARD PLAYABILITY VERDICT: Quick Battle / Gauntlet are finishable pointer-free end-to-end (menus → draft → battle turns → switching), EXCEPT in-battle item use. Story mode is NOT finishable pointer-free; blockers in flow order: (1) professor gift/starter card selection — hard block at the first required beat; (2) battle bag item+target selection — soft block (fights winnable itemless, but revives/potions unusable); (3) minigame overlays — passable but focus never enters the aria-modal dialog; (4) The Pits fighter picks — optional facility, hard-blocked; (5) all tooltip-borne info (move/ability/item/type details) unreachable — known ledgered. Biggest win per effort: copy the 3-line draft-card pattern (role=button + tabIndex=0 + keydown) onto prof-pick-card, story-bag-item, bag party-slot, and data-pits-pick rows, and add focus/Escape to _mgMountOverlay mirroring _showStoryTutorialScene.

The Quick-Battle draft cards (battle.html:20232-20234) already implement the correct pattern (role=button, tabIndex=0, aria-label, Enter/Space keydown) — the professor picker never received it. Every professor/mystery gift through the run is affected, starting with the starter.
